The line segment shown in the $xy$-plane represents one of the legs of a right triangle. The area of this triangle is $36sqrt(17)$ square units.

What is the length, in units, of the other leg of this triangle?
explanation: Choice C is correct. The line segment has endpoints at $(-5, 2)$ and $(7, 5)$. Using the distance formula, the length of this segment is $\sqrt{(7 - (-5))^{2} + (5 - 2)^{2}} = \sqrt{12^{2} + 3^{2}} = \sqrt{144 + 9} = \sqrt{153} = 3\sqrt{17}$. Since this segment is one leg of a right triangle with area $36\sqrt{17}$ square units, using the formula $A = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{leg}_{1} \times \text{leg}_{2}$ gives $36\sqrt{17} = \frac{1}{2} \times 3\sqrt{17} \times \text{leg}_{2}$. Multiplying both sides by $2$ yields $72\sqrt{17} = 3\sqrt{17} \times \text{leg}_{2}$. Dividing both sides by $3\sqrt{17}$ gives $\text{leg}_{2} = 24$.
